key_insight: Thermal conductivity in Cu-embedded g-C3N4 falls at intermediate cavity occupation and partially recovers near full occupation because low- and high-frequency phonon contributions compete.
engineering_relevance: Controlling metal occupation of intrinsic cavities offers a potential route to tuning in-plane heat transport in porous crystalline materials.
method: Homogeneous nonequilibrium molecular dynamics across cavity occupations
evidence_signal: Simulations show suppressed transport below 10 THz and a recovering contribution at 20–30 THz as Cu occupation increases, with similar trends for Ag.
watch_item: The abstract reports simulation results but no experimental validation of the occupation-dependent thermal response.
paper_title: Nonmonotonic In-Plane Thermal Transport in Metal-Embedded Graphitic Carbon Nitride
